22686415.source: ORIGIN (PMID 22686415) abstract: 'The use of n-3 fatty acids also had no significant effect on the rates of major vascular events (1034 patients [16.5%] vs. 1017 patients [16.3%]; hazard ratio, 1.01; 95% CI, 0.93 to 1.10; P=0.81)'. ENDPOINT CORRECTION (override): the abstract's stated PRIMARY outcome is 'death from cardiovascular causes' (HR 0.98), which is NOT our outcome; the abstract's MAJOR VASCULAR EVENTS result (our MACE endpoint) is HR 1.01. The generic 'primary outcome' keyword matched ORIGIN's CV-death primary sentence (appearing first), pooling the wrong endpoint; this override pins the correct major-vascular-events value.
22686415.verification: Verbatim from the ORIGIN abstract: major vascular events HR 1.01 (95% CI 0.93-1.10), 1034/6239 (16.5%) n-3 vs 1017/6266 (16.3%) placebo. Crude RR from the counts = (1034/6239)/(1017/6266) = 1.021, corroborating HR 1.01 (both null). Corrects an abstract mis-selection of ORIGIN's CV-death primary (0.98) as our MACE endpoint (cycle 75 early-page audit).

23656645.reason: declared absent (definition mismatch, cross-family definition audit): the stored 733/6239 vs 745/6266 is Rischio e Prevenzione's REVISED primary endpoint 'death from cardiovascular causes or admission to hospital for cardiovascular causes' (a broad CV-death-or-hospitalization composite), NOT the 3-point major-vascular-events (death/MI/stroke) our outcome names. The abstract states the INITIALLY specified 3-point primary was revised after a lower-than-expected event rate; the 3-point counts are not in the abstract. Refuse rather than pool a broader CV-hospitalization composite under a major-vascular-events label.
23656645.verification: abstract: 'The initially specified primary end point was the cumulative rate of death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, and nonfatal stroke. At 1 year, after the event rate was lower than expected, [revised] ... the primary end point occurred in 1478 of 12,505 ... 733 of 6239 ...' -- the 733/6239 belongs to the revised broad composite.

38184150.reason: declared absent (definition mismatch, cross-family definition audit): OMEGA-REMODEL's MACE is an idiosyncratic composite (all-cause death, heart-failure hospitalization, recurrent acute coronary syndrome, late CABG) with NO stroke and NO cardiovascular-death component, in a 6-month post-AMI cardiac-remodeling pilot -- not the death/MI/stroke major-vascular-events endpoint our outcome names. Refuse rather than pool a different composite under a MACE label.
38184150.verification: abstract: OMEGA-REMODEL, 'Consecutive patients with AMI randomized 1:1 to 6 months of O3-FA (4 g/daily) or placebo'; MACE HR 1.014 by ITT for a composite lacking stroke/CV-death (a remodeling-trial MACE definition).

21115589.source: SU.FOL.OM3 (PMID 21115589) full text (PMC2993045, Results / fig 4): 'Allocation to omega 3 fatty acids was not associated with any significant effect on major vascular events (81 v 76 patients, hazard ratio 1.08 (0.79 to 1.47), P=0.64; fig 4).' This is the omega-3 MAIN-EFFECT MARGINAL (omega-3 present vs absent, collapsed over the 2x2 B-vitamin allocation) on the trial's declared primary outcome (major cardiovascular events). Double-blind, placebo-controlled factorial; 2501 patients with a history of myocardial infarction, unstable angina, or ischaemic stroke (secondary prevention). Estimand-matched: major vascular events, HR, intention-to-treat, trial end.
21115589.verification: FULL-TEXT RECOVERY of a trial the abstract path declared absent ('factorial-design trial: no extraction sentence explicitly names the intervention'). The omega-3 marginal HR 1.08 (95% CI 0.79-1.47) is reported directly in the full text (PMC2993045) as the omega-3-vs-no-omega-3 main effect on major vascular events, the standard way a 2x2 factorial contributes a factor to a pairwise meta-analysis. Recovered after fixing _pmc_fulltext (which previously returned a citing article for non-primary PMIDs); 21115589 now correctly resolves to PMC2993045. Adding it moves omega-3 MACE from k=6 toward the null (1.08 > pooled 0.9353), not toward the intervention -- honest completeness, not a flattering addition.
